name: Abnormal Number of Coronary Ostia

criteria.description: Identification of abnormal number of coronary ostia via coronary angiography or CT coronary angiography
Presence of ischemic symptoms such as angina or exertional chest pain unexplained by other causes
Exclusion of other coronary artery anomalies or acquired coronary artery disease

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Imaging confirmation of abnormal coronary ostia number is required; clinical symptoms and exclusion of other causes support diagnosis
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis primarily relies on imaging modalities; clinical presentation varies widely.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Multiple coronary ostia detected on imaging
searchTerms: extra heart artery openings on imaging

pathognomonic.symptomName: Single coronary ostium with anomalous origin
searchTerms: single coronary artery with unusual origin
one coronary artery from wrong place

common.notes: Transient loss or near loss of consciousness

occasional.symptomName: Myocardial ischemia without coronary artery disease
occasional.notes: Ischemic changes on ECG or stress testing
searchTerms: heart muscle lack of oxygen without artery blockage

occasional.notes: Including ventricular tachycardia or atrial fibrillation

occasional.symptomName: Fatigue related to decreased cardiac output
searchTerms: fatigue due to low cardiac output

laboratory: Normal cardiac biomarkers unless ischemic injury present
Possible elevated troponin in ischemic events
imaging: Coronary angiography showing abnormal number or origin of coronary ostia
CT coronary angiography confirming ostial anomalies
Cardiac MRI for assessment of myocardial ischemia or fibrosis
genetic: No specific genetic markers identified; possible familial clustering in rare cases
other: Electrocardiogram abnormalities suggestive of ischemia or arrhythmia
Stress testing may reveal inducible ischemia

distinguishingFeatures: Single coronary ostium with anomalous artery course
Different ostial number but abnormal artery trajectory
Typical risk factors and progressive stenosis

redFlags: Sudden onset chest pain with syncope
Evidence of myocardial ischemia on ECG or biomarkers
Sudden cardiac arrest or unexplained syncope
references: Angelini P. Coronary artery anomalies: an entity in search of an identity. Circulation. 2007;115(10):1296-1305.
Yamanaka O, Hobbs RE. Coronary artery anomalies in 126,595 patients undergoing coronary arteriography. Cathet Cardiovasc Diagn. 1990;21(1):28-40.
